visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A male host wearing glasses and a black shirt stands in a professional studio setting. He uses animated facial expressions and hand gestures to discuss ear muscles. The background is dark with warm accent lighting and a bookshelf visible on the right. (2) A transition occurs to a detailed anatomical illustration of the human ear and skull, highlighting three specific muscles: Auricularis Anterior, Superior, and Posterior in yellow. These are labeled with technical text overlays. (3) The host returns to the frame, continuing his explanation with energetic hand movements. The lighting remains warm, focusing on his head and shoulders. (4) An insert image shows a close-up of a human ear with several medical electrodes and wires attached to the skin around the temple area, demonstrating how researchers monitor muscle signals. (5) A diagram showing the top-down view of an experimental setup appears, illustrating a participant surrounded by a screen and various speakers positioned at 0 to 180 degrees to test sound localization. (6) A statistical bar chart is presented, showing the 'Normalized Energy' of muscle signals across 'Easy', 'Medium', and 'Difficult' listening conditions, with the highest energy seen in the red 'Difficult' bar. (7) The host reappears, pointing to his head and gesturing toward the bottom of the screen to conclude the video and invite viewers to watch more content.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Subtitle]: 你身上那條最沒有用的肌肉. [Logo]: PanSci. (2) [Subtitle]: 其實可以用哦. (3) [Subtitle]: 你可以動你的耳朵嗎. (4) [Subtitle]: 我知道有少數人可以. (5) [Subtitle]: 但大部分人不行. (6) [Subtitle]: 人類其實有3條幫助耳朵轉動的肌肉. (7) [Subtitle]: 耳前肌、耳上肌、耳後肌. (8) [Subtitle]: 理論上，我們可以轉動耳朵的方向. (9) [Subtitle]: 對準聲音的來源. (10) [Subtitle]: 不僅能幫助你聽得更清楚. (11) [Subtitle]: 還能更準確辨認方位. (12) [Subtitle]: 只是隨著演化，在大部分的人類身上. (13) [Subtitle]: 這3條肌肉已經退化了. (14) [Subtitle]: 但有趣的來了. (15) [Subtitle]: 德國薩爾蘭大學的研究團隊發現. (16) [Subtitle]: 雖然這些肌肉看似已經失去作用. (17) [Subtitle]: 但當他們監測這3條肌肉. (18) [Subtitle]: 發現，在人耳聽到聲音的時候. (19) [Subtitle]: 耳上肌的肌電圖特別活躍. (20) [Subtitle]: 接著他們做了一個實驗. (21) [Subtitle]: 他們播放有聲書給受試者聽. (22) [Subtitle]: 並請他們嘗試聽清楚有聲書的內容. (23) [Subtitle]: 除此之外，旁邊會同時播放其他podcast作為噪音. (24) [Subtitle]: 當他們逐步增加旁邊podcast的數量與音量. (25) [Subtitle]: 結果發現，耳上肌的訊號增強了. (26) [Subtitle]: 也就是說，當人類需要把目標的聲音聽得更清楚時. (27) [Subtitle]: 上耳肌似乎就會更加活躍. (28) [Subtitle]: 另外他們也發現，當音源改變位置. (29) [Subtitle]: 也就是當耳朵需要辨別聲音方位的時候. (30) [Subtitle]: 耳後肌會特別活躍. (31) [Subtitle]: 只是雖然監測到了肌電圖的訊號. (32) [Subtitle]: 但實際上耳朵移動的幅度. (33) [Subtitle]: 小到沒有任何影響. (34) [Subtitle]: 有努力，但不多. (35) [Subtitle]: 至於這個研究是不是能有什麼後續. (36) [Subtitle]: 你看，既然神經訊號有了. (37) [Subtitle]: 透過腦機介面，加裝個電動耳朵. (38) [Subtitle]: 或是電競獸耳，是不是很不錯呢. (39) [Subtitle]: 話說馬斯克跟左克柏在腦機介面的投資力度都不小. (40) [Subtitle]: 馬斯克甚至願意自己植入晶片. (41) [Subtitle]: 你也想腦洞大開，隔空操物嗎. (42) [Subtitle]: 可以點這邊來看.
